extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, PTAB practitioners, and IP counsel involved in IPRs, district court patent litigation, ITC and federal claims
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes procedural and discretionary standards used by district courts, the PTAB, the Director, the Precedential Opinion Panel, the ITC, and the Court of Federal Claims in deciding stays, institution/denial of IPRs, Director review, sanctions, discovery, and related motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to lift a stay during appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may lift a stay during appeal where further delay would create undue prejudice (e.g., due to age of owner/primary witness), the appeal involves only a single claim (especially one affirmed previously), and substantial district-court progress (discovery begun, Markman hearing held) has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taken together these factors can warrant lifting a stay even while an appeal is pending; courts weigh undue prejudice, scope of the appeal, and case progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of motion to strike under Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(f)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to strike under Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(f)(2) must be filed within 21 days of the pleading that raises the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB proceedings or final written decisions do not excuse untimeliness; a motion based on information brought to light in PTAB decisions can still be untimely if filed after the 21-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-institution stay: need to show likelihood of institution
rubrics_metrics.description: For a stay requested before the PTAB decides whether to institute, a defendant must explain why institution is likely; speculative assertions of potential simplification are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if other stay factors (early stage, low prejudice) favor a stay, lack of persuasive demonstration that PTAB will institute (and thus simplify issues) weighs heavily against a pre-institution stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay when some patents have instituted IPRs and others denied
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts may stay litigation only as to patents that are subject to instituted IPRs and decline to stay patents where IPR was denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court considers simplification of issues, whether PTAB claim constructions bind the court, stage of the case, plaintiff's willingness to proceed on specific patents, and undue prejudice (e.g., small plaintiff vs large defendant, independence of infringement claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PTAB expert application to assess claim definiteness
rubrics_metrics.description: An expert’s prior application of a reference using a disputed claim term 'without any uncertainty' can support the conclusion that a skilled artisan would understand the claim term with reasonable certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior expert usage in IPRs can be persuasive in district court indefiniteness disputes; courts may rely on how experts applied terms in related PTAB proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateral estoppel dismissal based on PTAB IPR decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A court may dismiss an infringement complaint due to collateral estoppel when PTAB final written decisions held claims unpatentable and differences between asserted claims do not materially alter the invalidity question, and the other elements of collateral estoppel are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material similarity of the invalidity question is key; slight rewording of claims will not avoid collateral estoppel if the invalidity analysis is unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited preservation discovery in stayed litigation (good cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts may authorize limited discovery and preservation depositions during a stay upon a showing of good cause (e.g., volatile/transitory industry practices, risk of loss of evidence, high employee turnover, temporary field offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief can include requiring a defendant to produce top customers list, contact information, devices sold, quantities, preservation of sales records, and limited customer depositions where plaintiff shows risk of evidence loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasive (but non-preclusive) effect of vacated PTAB/CAFC decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions vacated for procedural reasons (e.g., because an agency lacked authority) may lack preclusive effect but can nonetheless be persuasive in later proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may independently assess the merits and may find vacated or reversed opinions persuasive even if those opinions are not binding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for staying litigation pending ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts consider stage of litigation (trial date, discovery completion), likelihood that reexamination will simplify or eliminate issues, and potential undue prejudice when deciding to stay pending reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stay is more likely where trial has not been set, discovery is incomplete, reexamination is likely to simplify issues, and prejudice considerations favor a stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: ITC judicial notice and exhibit list timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: The ITC may deny judicial notice of documents (e.g., foreign opposition notices, PTAB decisions) if they were not included on a party’s exhibit list and are untimely under applicable ground rules (e.g., Ground Rule 9.4.14.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untimely or unlisted documents are subject to denial even if sought for limited purposes such as identifying prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: ITC will not stay remedial orders based solely on ongoing PTAB proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The ITC distinguishes between instituted IPRs (or mere institution) and final written decisions; ongoing PTAB proceedings or mere institution do not by themselves justify staying remedial orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to stay remedial orders are more persuasive if based on final PTAB decisions rather than mere institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifying ITC protective order to use confidential information at PTAB (good cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking to amend a protective order to permit use of confidential information in PTAB proceedings must show good cause, cite precedent, and overcome Commission policy favoring production of confidential business information in Section 337 discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to cite precedent or to demonstrate why discovery cannot be obtained at the PTAB will weigh against modification; Commission policy disfavors amendments that would chill production of CBI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing/effect of fee payment via Treasury/Fedwire for §315(b) bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment wired to Treasury in accordance with USPTO instructions and confirmed by Fedwire (i.e., received by Treasury) constitutes sufficient evidence of timely payment for purposes of the one-year bar under §315(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treasury confirmation can show petitioner complied with the USPTO’s payment instructions even if USPTO did not receive funds until later; institution may still be denied on other substantive grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review: bases for sua sponte review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may initiate review sua sponte of Board institution or final decisions where the case raises novel issues of law or policy, issues of particular importance to the Office and the patent community, or concerns about abuse of process or discretionary denials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director review can be used to clarify application of precedent, address abuse of process, define policy approaches (e.g., General Plastic, Fintiv), and set briefing schedules for amici.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director guidance on applying General Plastic when first petition was discretionarily denied
rubrics_metrics.description: When the first-filed petition was discretionarily denied or not evaluated on the merits, General Plastic factors 1–3 only weigh in favor of discretionary denial if there are 'road-mapping' concerns under factor 3 or other concerns under factor 2; otherwise, a later-filed petition should be able to be decided on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director vacated denials where the Board applied General Plastic too broadly against joinder petitions following discretionary denials, emphasizing the Board’s mission to improve patent quality and balance against potential abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible timing for stipulations to reduce overlap with parallel litigation (Fintiv)
rubrics_metrics.description: A stipulation related to the Fintiv factor 4 analysis offered by a petitioner for the first time after a decision denying institution is not a proper basis for rehearing; stipulations should be offered prior to the Board’s institution decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid gamesmanship, the only appropriate time to offer stipulations limiting overlap with district-court litigation is before the Board decides whether to institute review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abuse of IPR process and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an IPR to extract payment, offering to not vigorously pursue a petition in exchange for payment, or engaging in discovery misconduct can constitute abuse of the IPR process and unethical conduct, warranting sanctions (e.g., preclusion from participating, show-cause orders, potential compensatory damages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director found abuse where a petitioner sought payment in relation to an IPR and sanctioned the petitioner and counsel, elevating other parties where appropriate and ordering the Board to evaluate the petition’s merits under heightened scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a 'compelling merits' standard in exceptional cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In unique fact patterns involving significant district-court investment and concerns about prior conflicting adjudications, the Director may require the Board to apply a heightened 'compelling merits' standard (rather than the usual 'reasonable likelihood' standard) at institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognizes the need to conserve judicial and Board resources and protects substantial district-court investments; the institution record must make very clear the need for USPTO involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: POP review denial with instruction to original panel
rubrics_metrics.description: The Precedential Opinion Panel may deny POP review but order the original Board panel, in considering rehearing, to address specific factual or legal issues inadequately treated in the original decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the record is fully developed on particular issues (e.g., public accessibility of references via research aids), POP may direct the panel to make the factual findings rather than taking POP review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sotera/Sand Revolution stipulations can overcome Fintiv in some cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipulations limiting potential overlap with parallel litigation (e.g., Sotera-type or Sand Revolution-type stipulations) can outweigh a trial-date gap and lead to institution, especially when petitioner demonstrates diligence and substantively strong grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board balances trial-date gap against petitioner diligence, timing of filing, strength of grounds, and the scope/reach of the stipulation in deciding Fintiv issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic grounds for denying subsequent petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Second petitions challenging the same patent claims may be denied under General Plastic where factors favor denial: petitioner delayed filing despite knowledge of the prior art, refined grounds based on prior proceedings (road-mapping), or inefficiency given a previously instituted IPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a second petition after a preliminary response to the first, or after learning additional information, can weigh strongly for denial absent compelling justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reusing expert declarations across proceedings—when allowed or disallowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Reusing another party’s earlier expert declaration without demonstrating cooperation or availability can lead to denial (particularly if the declarant has an exclusive engagement); however, reusing a declaration may be acceptable if facts differ (no exclusivity) and there is reason to think the declarant would participate and be subject to cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards scrutinize reused declarations for credibility and cooperation; relying heavily on a declaration while showing no ability to procure the declarant’s testimony is an anti-pattern that can justify denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv denial factors including trial-date gap, timing, and stipulation adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating a petition under Fintiv, the Board considers the gap between trial date and projected final written decision, the timing of the petition (e.g., filing on the time-bar date), and whether a petitioner’s stipulation meaningfully reduces overlap with district-court litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short trial gaps may still lead to denial if the petition was filed only at the time bar by 'mere hours' or stipulations do not meaningfully reduce overlap; conversely, timely filings with strong stipulations and diligence can overcome sizeable gaps.
